summary:
3in 7orus (Eye of Horus) is a maritime defense and environmental intelligence platform guarding Egypt’s Mediterranean coast, from Alexandria and the Nile Delta to the Suez Canal. When ships switch off tracking beacons at night or under clouds to dump oil or threaten undersea internet cables, normal cameras go blind. 3in 7orus sees through the dark.
Rather than waiting for external reports, 3in 7orus analyzes live NASA radar images right in the browser, separates real oil from calm-water illusions, and checks space weather so solar storms are never mistaken for deliberate blackouts. Whenever a ship goes silent past 30 minutes or lingers over an undersea cable, the system maps a current-driven search zone, predicts the next radar satellite pass to catch it, backtracks spills to their origin, and forecasts when oil will reach ports, desalination plants, or beaches, sizing the exact floating barriers needed.
Inside its isolated 24-hour Historical Replay and Forensic Lab, 3in 7orus recreates real Egyptian spills from 2004 to 2021. Had it existed then, early warning could have prevented $8M to $22M per incident in cleanup, port delays, and ecological loss. Looking ahead, 3in 7orus safeguards Suez trade, global internet cables, fisheries, and tourism, offering interactive blackout and spill simulators, custom case uploads, multi-layer maps, and one-click evidence reports.
details:
3in 7orus (Eye of Horus) - Med-East Orbital Command is a maritime security and marine pollution intelligence platform that protects the Egyptian Eastern Mediterranean corridor, covering Alexandria and the Nile Delta through to the northern approach to the Suez Canal. When vessels switch off their tracking beacons (AIS) at night or beneath cloud cover to dump illegal oil or threaten critical undersea internet cables, optical satellites and coastal receivers lose sight of them. That gap matters. 3in 7orus brings back continuous awareness by combining spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), live vessel telemetry, space weather and ocean-weather physics in one command map.

In Live Coastal Surveillance mode, 3in 7orus pulls live NASA ASF Sentinel-1 radar quicklook imagery and runs a custom Dual-Pol 2D Hysteresis CFAR detector right in the user's browser through HTML5 Canvas, with no need for specialized server GPUs. It runs locally. The system automatically masks land, Nile Delta coastal lagoons and swath-edge noise, then pulls out slick geometry and radar contrast (dB), filters calm-water illusions and checks detections against SkyTruth Cerulean.

rages gets fixed at its Last Known Position. Then an expanding 360-degree evasive reachability disk, pushed by ocean currents, and a directional search cone are applied. A Subsea Cable Watchdog keeps watch over major fiber-optic corridors like SEA-ME-WE 5, AAE-1 and FLAG Europe-Asia. It flags vessels that linger slowly at 0.2-5.0 kts or move within 3.0 km of cable buffers. Using live NORAD orbital elements and satellite.js (SGP4), 3in 7orus projects Sentinel-1A, Sentinel-1C and NISAR-01 24 hours forward to find the next satellite capture window. It also calculates azimuth Doppler velocity shifts to check a vessel's true speed.

For rapid containment, 3in 7orus mixes real-time wind, wave and ocean current data from a 3-buoy grid at Alexandria, Damietta and Port Said. The goal is direct. It traces oil slicks back to their source and predicts coastal landfall 24 hours ahead, marking harbors, desalination intakes, wetlands and shipping approaches at risk. It also sizes the exact number of meters of floating containment booms needed. On top of that, it models USD financial liability across 10,000-run ranges.

Inside its isolated Forensic Case Lab, analysts can move through a 24-hour historical replay, minute by minute, of five documented Eastern Mediterranean spills from 2004-2021 using archived weather data and satellite swaths. They can upload custom JSON incident cases. They can test interactive blackout and oil-spill simulations, switch between four basemaps including Satellite, Dark Radar, Nautical Chart and NASA VIIRS, then turn on six tactical overlays. Exports are available too. The lab can produce court-ready and responder-ready Official Forensic Dossiers in JSON, TXT or printable formats.

Historical reconstructions in our Forensic Lab put median damages at $8M to $22M+ for each major spill, counting shoreline cleanup, maritime corridor delays and marine habitat loss. The costs stack up fast. If 3in 7orus had been running during past Eastern Mediterranean incidents from 2004 to 2021, early warnings and targeted boom deployment could have stopped tens of millions of dollars in cascading damage.

Looking ahead, continuous orbital monitoring helps protect global maritime trade corridors and multi-terabit undersea internet infrastructure. It also covers coastal fisheries, desalination plants and tourism. Maritime authorities, port operators, cable operators and environmental response teams get fast, usable intelligence in one click.

We built the frontend with TypeScript, React 19, HTML5 Canvas, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, satellite.js, Motion, Lucide Icons and Vite. On the backend, a Node.js and Express (tsx) proxy with a caching layer keeps things moving. The whole platform runs on standard consumer laptops and cloud web containers.

During development, our team built safeguards for real radar failure modes. Some were tricky. We filter low-wind (< 3 kts) look-alikes and high-sea-state (> 16 kts) wave dispersion, check NASA DONKI and NOAA Kp space weather along with nearby vessel VHF reception to rule out solar effects or coverage dropouts, apply a ~3.9 km shoreline clearance mask to avoid false detections over Nile Delta lakes, keep historical and simulation state separate from live alerts and provide cached fallbacks that keep the system running without interruption.
